notes.title: Feb 2023 Patch
notes.content:
[b]Main Change[/b]
After digging through every aspect I could possibly think of, the cause for the "Chase Squirrels" crash should be completely resolved. This was a very difficult issue to find because it only occurs on certain hardware. Now (thankfully), I believe I have located (and removed) the cause. I cannot be 100% sure though, since I have been unable to recreate the issue on my own hardware. If you still encounter the issue after this update, please let me know!

[b]Other Changes[/b]
[list]
[*]Fixed neighbor's dog not hunting when loading from a checkpoint in Chapter 5.
[*]Significantly shortened sequences in Chapters 3, 6, and 7.
[*]Significantly increased the time your exploration in Chapter 7 will go unaffected by surrounding threats.
[*]Added clarification to commonly confusing points in Chapter 7.
[/list]
I am aware that this update may not address all the issues that players have noted while playing the game, but please be patient with me as I learn from the mistakes I made during the development of this game. This is my first ever experience releasing a game to the public, and the scale (from the main campaign to the extras) is massive for a first-time solo indie dev doing this in his free time. Some requests (as simple as they may sound on the surface) may take much longer than anticipated to implement into the game due to this scale.

As I have addressed in other threads, some elements working together may cause one bug, but that bug may be preventing several others. It's something I'm trying to work out little by little as time goes on!

I will continue to make changes and update elements as I find the time. Either way, I appreciate all the criticism (as intense as some of it may be) and I am using it all to improve myself as a developer moving forward!

Thank you for your patience and understanding!

notes.title: Coming Bug Fixes and Updates
notes.content:
I wanted to provide an update regarding the known issues with BARK and what you can expect in the coming updates.

[list]
[*]Chapter 4 checkpoints not working (garage door trigger did not work and first radio broadcast plays despite having completed that segment already). This is also often followed by your owner being unable to open the door to the garage. This checkpoint currently requires a restart of the chapter.
[*]Your owner will occasionally get stuck in doorways while searching for you. This will sometimes result in him de-spawning. Know that this is not intended, and whenever your owner searches for you, he is intended to eventually return to one of two rooms and close the door behind him.
[*]If a dog in the neighborhood is too far away but is trying to start a chase, the chase music will start despite not actually chasing you.
[*]The game occasionally crashes (most often during Chapter 5 (the backyard chapter)) for unknown reasons. This has only happened to some players with a variety of hardware, so I have so far been unable to find probable cause.
[*]Various functions and solutions to objectives are not clear. More hints will be added to better explain what can be done during these circumstances.
[/list]

As far as I am currently aware, this is the extent of remaining issues. These fixes will be made intermittently as I work towards the (currently unannounced) DLC. If the file-size for the game increases any significant amount during these updates, it is due to the DLC content that is being added to the game.

Thank you all for your continued support and understanding while I work through the post-release beast that is BARK!

notes.title: BARK 1.4 (Difficulty Adjustments and Clarity Patch)
notes.content:
[list]
[*]Adjusted the way the neighboring dog responds to being barked at. It will no longer chase you when barked at if it is not currently barking. This was a common misunderstanding related to how to evade the neighboring dog and has now been modified to better fit players' expectations.
[*]Increased the time between the neighboring dog stopping to scan for you in chapter 7.
[*]Increased the amount of time the neighboring dog will bark at you before chasing you in chapter 7.
[*]Added the ability to escape a chase with the neighboring dog. This was initially not intended to increase the steaks when roaming the neighborhood, but I can see how inconvenient and frustrating this can be when trying to explore.
[*]Increased the buffer period when your owner stops to listen for your movement.
[*]Added and modified various hints to better help explain certain objectives in chapters 5 and 7.
[*]Added a hint regarding achieving one of the 3 available endings after completing the game once.
[*]Added the ability to enable and disable the display of hints and tutorials at will.
[*]Fixed a bug where the objective "Get into the garage." would trigger despite having already entered the garage in Chapter 4.
[/list]

NOTE: These changes have been made to make the game a more fluid and enjoyable experience. I have been made aware that the game is commonly agreed to be too difficult. I considered adding difficulty settings, but the challenge of the game plays its own part in the story. Removing or allowing the player to determine how challenging the game is will detract from the intended experience. Instead, I will continue to update the difficulty as necessary to appeal to as many players as I can! I am also aware and currently researching the reasons for crashes (most commonly seen in Chapter 5). I am unsure what is causing this, but will continue to search for solutions!

notes.title: MID AUGUST UPDATES
notes.content:
As the end of August approaches, it is clear that I will have to delay the release of BARK one more time. Because I am working on this project by myself for 10-14 hours every day, I struggled through about 2 weeks of pure burnout and demotivation to complete the project. Of course, this being said, I am back on track and development is continuing as it was before.

This period of burnout was not completely unproductive though, in fact a lot of cleanup and polish has been done. The game's core mechanics function much better and smoother; A few frame rate issues have been adjusted to fit a more wide variety of devices; Some lighting issues have been worked out; And a select group of sound effects have been reworked to enhance the scariness of the experience. Overall, the experience has been enhanced and polished a LOT.

[b]So when should I expect BARK to be released?[/b]
Although I am forcing myself to not rush this project nor set unrealistic goals for myself, I aiming for BARK to be released by the end of September. The specific date is not set because it can vary due to Steam's review process, but expect BARK to be fully complete and released by the end of September!

[list]
[*] Some personal motivation issues have caused for another delay
[*] Several in-game features and designs have been cleaned and polished
[*] Release date expectancy has been changed to Late September
[/list]

notes.title: EARLY JULY UPDATES
notes.content:
[h3][b]A continuation of unexpected setbacks and challenges have pushed release back to approximately late August.[/b][/h3]

As is stands currently, BARK is nearing completion of the main campaign. Although it had initially been planned to release in early June, conceptual and gameplay related changes, polish, and other crucial development processes led to the inevitable setback of release. This setback, however, was only able to result in the majority of the main campaign's completion. In other words, there is still a lot of work left before the game is ready to release.

Just because more content is being added to the game though, does not mean the game will differ from what is being showcased. The current features and screenshots provided on the game's page(s) are an accurate representation of the final product, and only minimal changes are likely to be seen moving forward.

[b]So why is the release of BARK being pushed back again?[/b]
The main campaign of the game is in its final stages. With exclusion of these final steps, it is polished and ready for release. This being said, all extras have yet to be created. The inclusion of extra gameplay outside of the main campaign was a recent addition to the development checklist, but will result in a more fulfilling and rewarding experience overall.

[list]
[*] Features and screenshots are confirmed to officially reflect the final product
[*] Extra gameplay features outside of the main campaign have been confirmed
[*] Release date expectancy has been changed to Late August
[/list]

notes.title: EARLY JUNE UPDATES
notes.content:
[h3][b]After some interesting challenges, it looks like BARK is on track to release in mid July![/b][/h3]

This will be my first official game release to Steam, so please bare with me as I finish development and adapt to changes I am forced to make along the way. The game was originally planned to release near the end of June, however Steam's summer sale will be underway at that time. I have decided that it is best to release once the sale has concluded to allow for Steam's typical boost in viewership of new releases.

This being said, development plans and gameplay features have not changed (besides some adjustments to the game's visuals) meaning BARK is well on its way to completion. You may have noticed the change in graphical style from pixelated to stylized. This, I believe anyway, aids to the game better fitting in a "modern" design, which was the original intent.

BARK still has a lot of development left to go, and I will be working non-stop to get it ready for release by mid July. Expect more updates over the coming weeks as development concludes and I cannot wait to see all of the terror and dog treats finally meet your screens!

[*] Release date has been changed to Mid July
[/list]
